description: Individual keyboard and mouse-modifier shortcuts of the draw.io editor, taken from the editor's key bindings (grapheditor and diagramly EditorUi) and the official shortcut sheet. On macOS Cmd replaces Ctrl and Option replaces Alt. Each entry names the action id so it can also be invoked through the embed protocol's invokeAction or remapped with the keyboardShortcuts configuration key.

tools.name: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Undo / Redo)
tools.description: Ctrl+Z undoes the last model change; Ctrl+Y (Windows) and Ctrl+Shift+Z (Linux/macOS, also Windows) redo it. The undo history covers cell edits, style changes, page operations and layouts but not view changes such as zoom or scroll. Actions: undo, redo.
tools.example: Apply Arrange > Layout > Organic, then press Ctrl+Z to restore the previous positions.
tools.notes: Inside the label editor the same keys undo text edits only. Edit > Undo/Redo show the same actions in the menu.

tools.name: Ctrl+X / Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V (Cut / Copy / Paste)
tools.description: Standard clipboard operations on the selected cells. Copied cells are serialised as draw.io XML on the system clipboard, so they can be pasted into another draw.io window, a text editor (as XML) or back onto the canvas offset from the original; pasting external images or text inserts image/text cells. Actions: cut, copy, paste.
tools.example: Select a group of shapes, Ctrl+C, switch to another diagram tab and Ctrl+V to reproduce them with their styles and connections.
tools.notes: Pasting at the mouse position instead of the viewport centre is enabled by the pasteAtMousePointer configuration key. The native clipboard can be disabled with enableNativeClipboard:false.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+X / Ctrl+Shift+V (Copy as Image / Paste unformatted text)
tools.description: Ctrl+Alt+X copies the selection (or the whole diagram when nothing is selected) to the clipboard as a PNG image for pasting into documents and chats; Ctrl+Shift+V pastes clipboard text without formatting while editing a label. Actions: copyAsImage, pasteUnformatted (label editor).
tools.example: Select three shapes, press Ctrl+Alt+X and paste the image into a Word document.
tools.notes: Edit > Copy as Image is the menu equivalent; the image uses the current theme colours.

tools.name: Ctrl+D / Ctrl+Enter (Duplicate)
tools.description: Creates a copy of the selected cells offset by the grid size and selects the copy; connected edges between duplicated cells are duplicated too. Ctrl+Enter does the same when not editing a label (while editing, it stops editing). Action: duplicate.
tools.example: Select a swimlane and press Ctrl+D to add an identical lane below it.
tools.notes: Ctrl+drag or Alt+drag clones interactively at any position.

tools.name: Delete / Backspace, Ctrl+Delete, Shift+Delete (Delete variants)
tools.description: Delete or Backspace removes the selected cells (edges attached to deleted vertices stay dangling); Ctrl+Delete / Ctrl+Backspace deletes the cells together with their connected edges; Shift+Delete / Shift+Backspace deletes only the labels of the selection. Actions: delete, deleteAll, deleteLabels.
tools.example: Select a node in a flow and press Ctrl+Delete to remove it and all its connectors in one step.
tools.notes: Cells with deletable=0 or locked cells are skipped. Edit > Delete with connections is the menu form of Ctrl+Delete.

tools.name: Ctrl+A / Ctrl+Shift+A (Select All / Select None)
tools.description: Ctrl+A selects every unlocked cell in the current layer group (inside a group when a group is entered); Ctrl+Shift+A clears the selection. Actions: selectAll, selectNone.
tools.example: Ctrl+A then Ctrl+Shift+Y to autosize every shape to its label.
tools.notes: Locked layers and cells with locked=1 are excluded.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+I / Ctrl+Shift+E (Select Vertices / Select Edges)
tools.description: Select all shapes (vertices) or all connectors (edges) of the current page, which is the fastest way to restyle every connector or every box at once through the Format panel. Actions: selectVertices, selectEdges.
tools.example: Ctrl+Shift+E, then set Waypoints to Curved in the Format panel to make every connector curved.
tools.notes: Edit > Select Vertices / Select Edges in the menu.

tools.name: Tab / Shift+Tab, Alt+Tab, Alt+Shift+X / C (selection navigation)
tools.description: Tab selects the next cell and Shift+Tab the previous one in model order; Alt+Tab (or Alt+Shift+P) selects the parent of the current selection; Alt+Shift+X selects the children of the selected container and Alt+Shift+C all descendants, with a sibling-selection variant on the shortcut sheet. Useful for keyboard-only editing and for reaching cells hidden under others.
tools.usage: Tab / Shift+Tab   |   Alt+Tab or Alt+Shift+P   |   Alt+Shift+X / Alt+Shift+C
tools.example: Click a lane inside a pool, press Alt+Tab to select the pool, then Ctrl+D to duplicate the whole pool.
tools.notes: Alt+Click selects the cell below the pointer when shapes overlap.

tools.name: Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+U (Group / Ungroup)
tools.description: Ctrl+G groups the selected cells into a new group cell (style group) that moves and resizes as one; Ctrl+Shift+U dissolves selected groups and restores the children to the parent layer. Arrange > Remove from Group takes single children out. Actions: group, ungroup.
tools.example: Select an icon and its caption, Ctrl+G, then move them together; Ctrl+Shift+U to separate again.
tools.notes: Groups are ordinary vertices with container=1; double-click enters the group for editing children (Ctrl+Shift+End) and Ctrl+Shift+Home exits.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+F / Ctrl+Shift+B (To Front / To Back)
tools.description: Moves the selected cells to the top or bottom of the z-order within their parent, changing the order of the mxCell elements in the XML. Actions: toFront, toBack.
tools.example: Draw a background rectangle after the shapes and press Ctrl+Shift+B to put it behind them.
tools.notes: Layers provide coarser stacking; z-order applies within a layer or group.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F / Ctrl+Alt+Shift+B (Bring Forward / Send Backward)
tools.description: Moves the selection one step up or down in the z-order instead of all the way to the front or back, for fine control of overlapping shapes. Actions: bringForward, sendBackward (Arrange > Bring Forward / Send Backward).
tools.example: With three overlapping cards, select the bottom one and press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F once to place it between the others.
tools.notes: Some Linux window managers intercept Ctrl+Alt+Shift combinations; use the Arrange menu there.

tools.name: Ctrl+L / Alt+Shift+L (Lock/Unlock / Edit Link)
tools.description: Ctrl+L toggles the lock on the selected cells (sets locked=1 with movable/resizable/rotatable/deletable/editable/connectable=0 so they cannot be changed or selected by rubber band); Alt+Shift+L opens the Edit Link dialog to attach a URL, page link or custom action to the selection. Actions: lockUnlock, editLink.
tools.example: Select the title block, press Ctrl+L so it cannot be moved accidentally; select a box and press Alt+Shift+L to link it to page 2.
tools.notes: Locked cells can still be selected by clicking; use Edit > Unlock or Ctrl+L again to release them.

tools.name: Ctrl+M / Ctrl+Shift+M (Edit Data / Edit Geometry)
tools.description: Ctrl+M opens Edit Data (custom properties, ID, placeholders checkbox) for the selected cell, or the diagram-level data when nothing is selected; Ctrl+Shift+M opens Edit Geometry to type exact left/top/width/height/rotation values. Actions: editData, editGeometry.
tools.example: Select a server icon, Ctrl+M, add ip=10.0.0.5, tick Placeholders and set the label to %ip%.
tools.notes: metaEdit=1 in the style makes double-click open Edit Data as well.

tools.name: Ctrl+E / Ctrl+Shift+D / Ctrl+Shift+R (Edit Style / Set as Default Style / Clear Default Style)
tools.description: Ctrl+E opens the Edit Style dialog with the raw style string of the selection; Ctrl+Shift+D makes the selected cell's style the default for new vertices or edges; Ctrl+Shift+R restores the built-in defaults. Actions: editStyle, setAsDefaultStyle, clearDefaultStyle.
tools.example: Style one connector with curved=1;endArrow=block, press Ctrl+Shift+D, and every new connector uses that style.
tools.notes: Default styles are stored in the browser/desktop settings, not in the file; the configuration keys defaultVertexStyle/defaultEdgeStyle set them centrally.

tools.name: Alt+Shift+Q / Alt+Shift+W (Copy Style / Paste Style)
tools.description: Copies the style string of the selected cell to an internal buffer and applies it to other selected cells, acting as a format painter without the clipboard. Actions: copyStyle, pasteStyle (Edit > Copy Style / Paste Style).
tools.usage: Alt+Shift+Q on the source cell   |   Alt+Shift+W on the target cells
tools.example: Select the approved green box, Alt+Shift+Q, select ten other boxes, Alt+Shift+W.
tools.notes: Only style keys are transferred, not geometry, label or data. Copy Size / Paste Size handle dimensions.

tools.name: Alt+Shift+F / Alt+Shift+V (Copy Size / Paste Size)
tools.description: Alt+Shift+F remembers the width and height of the selected vertex and Alt+Shift+V applies that size to every selected vertex, which is the quick way to make a set of shapes identical in size. Actions: copySize, pasteSize (Arrange > Copy Size / Paste Size).
tools.example: Select the largest card, Alt+Shift+F, select all cards, Alt+Shift+V.
tools.notes: Arrange > Match Size in the Format panel does the same for a multi-selection relative to the first selected cell.

tools.name: Alt+Shift+B / Alt+Shift+E (Copy Data / Paste Data)
tools.description: Copies the custom attributes (Edit Data properties) of the selected cell and pastes them onto other cells, merging with existing properties. Handy for propagating metadata such as owner, status or link across many shapes. Actions: copyData, pasteData.
tools.example: Set owner=Ops on one node (Ctrl+M), Alt+Shift+B, select the other nodes, Alt+Shift+E.
tools.notes: The label attribute is not copied; placeholders resolve against the pasted values.

tools.name: Alt+Shift+T / Alt+Shift+N (Edit Tooltip / Edit Note)
tools.description: Alt+Shift+T opens the Edit Tooltip dialog (stored as the tooltip attribute and shown on hover in editor and viewer); Alt+Shift+N opens the note editor for a longer rich-text note attached to the cell (note attribute, shown with an icon in the viewer when showNoteIcons is enabled). Actions: editTooltip, editNote.
tools.example: Select a database shape, Alt+Shift+T and enter "PostgreSQL 16, primary".
tools.notes: Tooltips can contain placeholders when the cell has placeholders enabled.

tools.name: Alt+Shift+R (Clear Waypoints)
tools.description: Removes all manual waypoints from the selected edges so the edge style routes them automatically again; with a straight edge it resets to a direct line. Action: clearWaypoints (Arrange > Waypoints > Clear Waypoints).
tools.example: After moving shapes around, select all edges (Ctrl+Shift+E) and press Alt+Shift+R to re-route them cleanly.
tools.notes: Waypoints live in the mxGeometry's Array as="points".

tools.name: Alt+Shift+A / Alt+Shift+O (Connection Arrows / Connection Points)
tools.description: Alt+Shift+A toggles the blue hover arrows used for clone-and-connect (View > Connection Arrows); Alt+Shift+O toggles the display of fixed connection points (the blue crosses) when hovering shapes with an edge (View > Connection Points). Actions: connectionArrows, connectionPoints.
tools.example: Turn off connection arrows with Alt+Shift+A while positioning dense icon layouts, then turn them on again.
tools.notes: Per-shape suppression is available with the allowArrows=0 style key.

tools.name: Ctrl+B / Ctrl+I / Ctrl+U (Bold / Italic / Underline)
tools.description: With cells selected these toggle the fontStyle bits (1, 2, 4) of the whole label; inside the rich-text label editor they format the selected text with inline HTML instead. Actions: bold, italic, underline.
tools.example: Select all headers (Shift+click) and press Ctrl+B to make them bold.
tools.notes: Plain (non-HTML) labels only support whole-label formatting.

tools.name: Ctrl+. / Ctrl+, / Ctrl+Shift+Plus / Ctrl+Shift+Minus (Superscript, Subscript, Font size)
tools.description: Ctrl+. toggles superscript and Ctrl+, subscript on the selected text in the label editor; Ctrl+Shift+Plus and Ctrl+Shift+Minus (also Ctrl+} and Ctrl+{) increase or decrease the fontSize of the selected cells in steps. Actions: superscript, subscript, increaseFontSize, decreaseFontSize.
tools.example: Select every text cell and press Ctrl+Shift+Plus twice to enlarge all fonts.
tools.notes: Font size steps follow the sizes offered in the Format panel dropdown.

tools.name: Enter / F2 / Esc / Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter (label editing)
tools.description: Enter or F2 starts editing the label of the selected cell (typing any character also starts editing and replaces the label); Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Tab, F2 or Esc stop editing (Esc cancels the change); Shift+Enter inserts a line break in formatted labels while plain Enter inside the editor also adds a line (unless stopEditingOnEnter is configured). Actions: keyPressEnter, startEditing, stopEditing.
tools.usage: Enter / F2 (start)   |   Ctrl+Enter / Esc (stop)   |   Shift+Enter (new line)
tools.example: Select a box, type 'Order service' (editing starts automatically), press Ctrl+Enter to commit.
tools.notes: Double-clicking a shape also starts editing; double-clicking empty canvas opens the shape picker (shape-picker=0 disables it).

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+H / Ctrl+J / Ctrl+Shift+J (Fit Window / Fit Page / Fit Two Pages)
tools.description: Zoom presets: Ctrl+Shift+H scales the diagram so the whole drawing fits the window, Ctrl+J fits one page and Ctrl+Shift+J two pages side by side (page view). Actions: fitWindow, fitPage, fitTwoPages (View menu).
tools.example: After importing a large CSV, press Ctrl+Shift+H to see the entire result.
tools.notes: View > Fit Width is menu-only. The embed action fit does the same from a host page.

tools.name: Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+Plus / Ctrl+Minus / Alt+Wheel (Custom Zoom / Zoom In / Zoom Out)
tools.description: Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus zoom in and out by the zoomFactor (default 1.2); Ctrl+0 opens the Custom Zoom dialog to type a percentage; Alt+Wheel (or Ctrl+Wheel / Ctrl+Shift+Wheel and pinch on touch devices) zooms around the pointer. Actions: zoomIn, zoomOut, customZoom.
tools.example: Press Ctrl+0, type 150 and Enter for a 150 % view.
tools.notes: zoomWheel:true in the configuration lets the plain wheel zoom. The numeric keypad + and - work as well.

tools.name: Home / Shift+Home / End (Reset View / Home / Refresh)
tools.description: Home (or Enter with nothing selected) resets the view to 100 % and scrolls to the origin; Shift+Home is the Home action that scrolls to the page origin without changing zoom; End refreshes (revalidates) the rendering, useful after editing XML in Edit Diagram or when a shape looks stale. Actions: resetView, home, refresh.
tools.example: Press Home after zooming into a corner to get back to the default view.
tools.notes: View > Reset View in the menu.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+L / Ctrl+Shift+O / Ctrl+Shift+P / Ctrl+Shift+K / Ctrl+K (panel toggles)
tools.description: Show or hide the editor panels: Ctrl+Shift+L Layers, Ctrl+Shift+O Outline, Ctrl+Shift+P Format panel, Ctrl+Shift+K Shapes (sidebar) and Ctrl+K Tags. Actions: layers, outline, format, toggleShapes, tags (View menu).
tools.example: Press Ctrl+Shift+P and Ctrl+Shift+K to hide both side panels for a wider canvas during a presentation.
tools.notes: Panel visibility is remembered in the editor settings; the format=0 and sidebar=0 URL parameters hide them per session.

tools.name: Ctrl+F (Find/Replace)
tools.description: Opens the Find/Replace window that searches labels (and optionally metadata) across the page with plain text or regular expressions, selects matches one by one and can replace text in labels. Action: findReplace (Edit > Find/Replace).
tools.example: Ctrl+F, search 'v1.2', replace with 'v1.3', Replace All.
tools.notes: Enable 'Regular expression' for pattern matching; 'Match case' and 'Whole word' narrow results.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+G (Toggle Grid)
tools.description: Shows or hides the background grid (mxGraphModel grid attribute); snapping still follows the grid size while the grid is hidden unless Alt is held during drags. Action: grid (View > Grid).
tools.example: Hide the grid with Ctrl+Shift+G before taking a screenshot with Ctrl+Alt+X.
tools.notes: Grid size and colour are set in the Format panel Diagram tab.

tools.name: Ctrl+P / Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Shift+S (Print / Save / Save As)
tools.description: Ctrl+P opens the Print dialog (fit to pages, scale, page range); Ctrl+S saves to the current storage (in embed mode it triggers the save event, or saveAndExit when configured); Ctrl+Shift+S opens Save As to choose a name, format and storage location. Actions: print, save, saveAs.
tools.example: Ctrl+Shift+S, choose 'Editable SVG (.svg)' to save the diagram as a .drawio.svg for a Git repository.
tools.notes: With autosave enabled Ctrl+S is rarely needed; on the desktop app it writes a .bkp backup before overwriting.

tools.name: Ctrl+R (Turn / Rotate 90 degrees)
tools.description: Rotates the selected shapes by 90 degrees clockwise, using the direction key for shapes that support it and the rotation key otherwise; for edges it flips the orientation of the elbow. Action: turn (Arrange > Direction > Rotate 90 / Turn).
tools.example: Select a horizontal swimlane pool and press Ctrl+R to make it vertical.
tools.notes: Clicking the rotation handle also rotates by 90 degrees; dragging it rotates freely (Shift snaps to 15 degrees).

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+Y (Autosize)
tools.description: Resizes the selected vertices to fit their labels once (respecting whiteSpace=wrap so wrapped text grows in height). Action: autosize (Arrange > Autosize); the autosize=1 style key makes it automatic after every edit.
tools.example: Paste long names into several boxes, select them and press Ctrl+Shift+Y.
tools.notes: Table cells and containers with child layouts resize according to their layout rules instead.

tools.name: Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End / Ctrl+Shift+Home / Ctrl+Shift+End (Collapse / Expand / Exit Group / Enter Group)
tools.description: Ctrl+Home collapses and Ctrl+End expands the selected containers (fold state); Ctrl+Shift+End enters the selected group so its children can be edited in isolation and Ctrl+Shift+Home exits back to the parent. Actions: collapse, expand, enterGroup, exitGroup (Arrange > Navigation).
tools.example: Select every tree root (Tab through them) and press Ctrl+Home to fold the org chart to its top level.
tools.notes: Folding requires collapsible=1 (default for swimlanes) and defaultFoldingEnabled in the configuration.

tools.name: A / S / D / F / C / L / R / X (quick insert keys)
tools.description: With the canvas focused and no label being edited, single letters insert shapes at the mouse position: A text, S note (sticky), D rectangle, F ellipse, C connector/line, L link, R rhombus, X toggles freehand drawing mode. Actions: insertText, insertNote, insertRectangle, insertEllipse, insertEdge, insertLink, insertRhombus, insertFreehand.
tools.usage: A   |   S   |   D   |   F   |   C   |   L   |   R   |   X
tools.example: Hover over an empty area and press D, type a label, press Ctrl+Enter, then press C to start a connector.
tools.notes: The inserted shape uses the current default style. In the label editor these letters simply type text.

tools.name: Arrow keys with modifiers (move, resize, clone and connect, scroll)
tools.description: Cursor keys move the selection by 1 px (or scroll the canvas when nothing is selected); Shift+Cursor moves by one grid step (or switches page in page view with no selection); Ctrl+Cursor resizes by 1 px and Ctrl+Shift+Cursor by one grid step; Alt+Shift+Cursor clones the selected shape in that direction and connects the clone with an edge; Alt+Cursor scrolls the page.
tools.example: Select a process box and press Alt+Shift+Right three times to build a chain of four connected boxes.
tools.notes: Clone-and-connect uses the current default edge style and the direction of the arrow key.

tools.name: Ctrl+Shift+PgUp / Ctrl+Shift+PgDown (Previous / Next Page)
tools.description: Switches to the previous or next page tab of a multi-page file without using the mouse. With page view enabled and nothing selected, Shift+Cursor keys also scroll between printed pages of the current diagram.
tools.example: Press Ctrl+Shift+PgDown repeatedly to review every page before exporting a PDF with all pages.
tools.notes: Page tabs can be reordered by drag and renamed by double-click; links to pages use data:page/id.

tools.name: Ctrl+Alt+T (Run Last Layout)
tools.description: Re-runs the layout that was last executed from Arrange > Layout (or the CSV/embed layout) on the current selection or page, so a diagram can be re-arranged after adding nodes without navigating the menu again. Action: runLastLayout.
tools.example: Apply Arrange > Layout > Vertical Tree once; after adding three nodes press Ctrl+Alt+T.
tools.notes: Available in recent versions; the action appears in Arrange > Layout as 'Run Last Layout'.

tools.name: Space+Drag / Right-drag / Shift+Wheel / Alt+Ctrl+Shift+Drag (canvas navigation and space)
tools.description: Hold Space (or the right mouse button) and drag to pan the canvas; the wheel scrolls vertically and Shift+Wheel horizontally; Alt+Ctrl+Shift+Drag on empty canvas inserts or removes space, pushing everything on one side of the drag start apart or together (Arrange > Insert space).
tools.usage: Space+Drag or Right-click+Drag   |   Wheel / Shift+Wheel   |   Alt+Ctrl+Shift+Drag
tools.example: Alt+Ctrl+Shift+drag downward between two rows of a flowchart to make room for a new row.
tools.notes: On touch devices drag with one finger on empty canvas to pan and pinch to zoom.

tools.name: Alt / Shift / Ctrl modifiers while moving, resizing and selecting
tools.description: Alt+Resize or Alt+Move ignores grid snapping; holding Alt also ignores handles under the mouse so a drag starts on the shape; Shift+Resize keeps proportions; Ctrl+Resize resizes around the centre; Ctrl+Drag (or Alt+Drag on some platforms) clones instead of moving and Shift+Drag constrains movement to one axis; Alt+Drag from inside a shape starts a rubber-band selection and Alt+Drag with Shift selects intersecting cells; Alt+Click selects the cell below; Ctrl+Click or Shift+Click toggles a cell in the selection.
tools.usage: Alt+Resize/Move   |   Shift+Resize   |   Ctrl+Resize   |   Ctrl+Drag / Shift+Drag   |   Alt+Drag   |   Alt+Click   |   Ctrl/Shift+Click
tools.example: Ctrl+drag an icon to copy it; hold Shift while dragging to keep the copy aligned on the same row.
tools.notes: Dropping a shape onto an edge with the default settings splits the edge; hold Alt to disable replace/connect on drop targets.

tools.name: Hover arrows, rotation handle and library click modifiers
tools.description: Hover arrows: click clones the shape in that direction and connects it (Ctrl+Click clones without connecting, Shift+Click connects to an existing shape), drag draws a connector (Ctrl+Drag clones while connecting). Rotation handle: click rotates 90 degrees clockwise, drag rotates freely. Sidebar library shapes: click inserts the shape and connects it to the selected shape (or attaches it to the free end of a selected edge), Shift+Click replaces the selected shape with the clicked one, Alt+Click inserts and connects while Alt+Shift ignores the current default style, and Alt+Drag from the library disables replace/connect on drop targets. When dropping or pasting files, Ctrl asks how to insert, Alt inserts at the origin and Shift inserts as an image.
tools.usage: Hover arrow: Click / Ctrl+Click / Shift+Click / Drag   |   Rotation handle: Click / Drag   |   Library: Click / Shift+Click / Alt+(Shift+)Click / Alt+Drag
tools.example: Select a Start ellipse, then click a Process shape in the sidebar: it is inserted to the right and connected automatically.
tools.notes: The shape picker popup that opens on hover-arrow clicks can be disabled with ?shape-picker=0 or the shapePicker configuration key.
